about: Batch refusal vectors for invalid_command: the hub, at enqueue (set_workspace).
Authored in canopy (tests/canopy_mcp/fixtures/workspace/); every other holder keeps a byte-identical copy of the whole directory.
ASCII-only, no trailing whitespace, exactly one final newline.
Replay: a fresh hub minted with epoch e1 and an injectable clock at 0 ms; steps run in order. Window X's windowId is w-X.
Actors: window:A, window:B (a viewer window: its HTTP calls and its event stream), agent (the MCP tools, in process), clock.

window actions: claim {seq, shown, state, ifVacant?} (POST <ws>/claim; ifVacant = ?if_vacant=1); report {seq, shown, state} (PUT <ws>/active); goodbye (DELETE <ws>/active?window=w-X); connect (GET <ws>/events?window=w-X: status and the events delivered at once); receive (the events the open stream got since the last connect or receive, pings left out); disconnect (the stream ends); result {batch, seq, state, results} (POST <ws>/active/w-X/result).
agent actions: get_workspace; set_workspace {commands, base?, batch_id?, wait_s}. wait_s 0 returns at once. clock: advance {ms}.
state '$sample' is state.sample.json's state, '$empty' the empty state (tabs [], active null, layout null, zoom {}, instances {}, toolMru [], labels {}).

expect matches partially: an object matches when every key it names matches (recursively); a list matches element by element and has the same length; other values are equal. An absent expect asserts nothing.

Hub rules the steps pin: ids b-e1-<n> and c-e1-<n> count from 1 and only an accepted batch mints them; a refused batch has id null and results []; a pending batch reports results []; a window holds at most one delivered, unresolved batch and the next is delivered when it resolves; a delivered batch's deadline is delivery + 10 s, after which its unresolved commands are lost; an undelivered batch is delivered only before enqueue + 10 s and is expired from then on; window_gone 3 s after the stream ends without a new one, or at once when another window claims; a window's new stream replaces its old one, without window_gone and without delivering a delivered batch again; the hub checks base.window, never base.seq.
Each case runs on a fresh hub; its steps start with the setup they need (most: window A claims, shown, and connects).
A refused batch returns the current document beside batch {id: null, status: refused, reason, results: []}.

The hub owns every syntactic bound, one case or more per bound (bound names it): command-count (1..20), command-shape ({cmd, args?} only, args an object), verb-enum, edge-enum, mode-enum, step-enum, tool-enum, arg-type, arg-required, arg-unknown, arg-exclusive, macro-count (<= 16), macro-length (values <= 64), macro-charset (values printable ASCII 0x21-0x7E, names non-empty), query-bytes (<= 4096 UTF-8 bytes), zoom-percent (integer 10..400), base-shape ({window: string, seq: integer}), batch-id-type. A case whose expect is pending is the accepted side of its bound.
